requirements.text: Any vehicle component that could change shape or position, other than suspension components or active devices to protect pedestrians, shall be set to its stowed position during measurements.
For a vehicle equipped with a deployable pedestrian protection system (DPPS), measurements shall be taken with the system undeployed.

If the vehicle is fitted with a badge, mascot or other structure that would bend back or retract under an applied load of maximum 100 N, this load shall be applied before and/or while measurements are taken.
When performing measurements, the vehicle shall be positioned in its normal ride attitude.

For vehicles whose bonnet top surface is inclined at 50° so that the straight edge makes continuous or multiple contact, the reference line shall be determined with the straight edge inclined rearwards at 40° from the vertical.

The bonnet leading edge reference line shall be determined using a straight edge 1,000 mm long, held parallel to the vertical longitudinal plane of the car, inclined rearwards by 50° from the vertical with its lower end 600 mm above the ground, traversed across and in contact with the bonnet leading edge.
The top edge of the bumper shall also be regarded as the bonnet leading edge if it is contacted by the straight edge during the reference line procedure.
The primary reference marks shall be within ±25 mm of the design position in the vertical (Z) axis.
The vehicle manufacturer shall specify the type of primary reference mark and the vertical (Z) position of each mark relative to the ground.
For a vehicle with a lower bumper height of 500 mm or greater, the front bumper shall be assessed with the upper legform requirements of paragraph 4.1.2.

For a vehicle with a lower bumper height of at least 425 mm and less than 500 mm, the front bumper shall be assessed with either the lower legform requirements of paragraph 4.1.1 or the upper legform requirements of paragraph 4.1.2, at the manufacturer's choice.
For a vehicle with a lower bumper height of less than 425 mm, the front bumper shall be assessed with the lower legform requirements of paragraph 4.1.1.

Compliance with the lower legform to bumper performance requirements of paragraph 5.1.1 shall be verified using the test impactor specified in paragraph 6.3.1.1 and the test procedures specified in paragraph 7.1.1.

Compliance with the upper legform to bumper performance requirements of paragraph 5.1.2 shall be verified using the test impactor specified in paragraph 6.3.1.2 and the test procedures specified in paragraph 7.1.2.
For bumper test widths nominated by the manufacturer up to a maximum of 264 mm in total (relaxation zone), the tibia bending moment shall not exceed 380 Nm.
When tested per 7.1.1 (flexible lower legform to bumper), the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament elongation shall not exceed 22 mm.
When tested per 7.1.1, the absolute value of dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm.
When tested per 7.1.1, the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament elongation shall not exceed 13 mm.
When tested per 7.1.2 (upper legform to bumper), the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5 kN.
When tested per 7.1.2, the bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm.
At the time of testing, the test facility and the vehicle or sub-system shall have a relative humidity of 40 ± 30 percent and a stabilized temperature of 20 ± 4 °C.
The test site shall consist of a flat, smooth and hard surface with a slope not exceeding 1 percent.
Either a complete vehicle or a cut-body shall be used for the test, adjusted to the conditions of 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.1.2.
The vehicle shall be in its normal ride attitude and either securely mounted on raised supports or at rest on a flat horizontal surface with the parking brake applied.

The cut-body shall include all parts of the vehicle front structure, all under-bonnet components and all components behind the windscreen that may be involved in a frontal impact with a vulnerable road user, and shall be securely mounted in the normal vehicle ride attitude.
All devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant test.
The manufacturer shall show that any pedestrian protection devices will act as intended in a pedestrian impact.
Vehicle components that can change shape or position and have more than one fixed shape or position (other than active pedestrian protection devices) shall comply in each fixed shape or position.
Each flexible lower legform impactor to bumper test shall be completed within two hours of the impactor being removed from the controlled storage area.
The target points selected for the lower legform impact tests shall lie within the bumper test area.

The lower legform impact velocity vector shall be in the horizontal plane and parallel to the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±2° in the horizontal and longitudinal planes at first contact.
The lower legform impactor axis shall be perpendicular to the horizontal plane, with roll and pitch angle tolerance of ±2° in the lateral and longitudinal planes.
The bottom of the lower legform impactor shall be 75 mm above the ground reference plane at first contact with the bumper, with a tolerance of ±10 mm.
When setting the height of the propulsion system, an allowance shall be made for the influence of gravity during the impactor's free flight.
The impactor shall be released to free flight at such a distance from the vehicle that test results are not influenced by contact with the propulsion system during rebound.
The lower legform impactor shall be in free flight at the moment of impact with the bumper.
At first contact the lower legform impactor shall have the intended orientation about its vertical axis for correct knee joint operation, with a yaw angle tolerance of ±5°.
At first contact the lower legform impactor centre line shall be within ±10 mm of the selected impact location.
During contact between the lower legform impactor and the vehicle, the impactor shall not contact the ground or any object that is not part of the vehicle.
The impact velocity of the lower legform impactor striking the bumper shall be 11.1 ± 0.2 m/s, taking the effect of gravity into account when derived from pre-contact measurements.
The tibia bending moments of the flexible lower legform impactor shall not exceed ±15 Nm within the 30 ms evaluation interval immediately prior to impact.
Offset compensation shall be done with the flexible lower legform impactor in resting position prior to the test/acceleration phase.
Each upper legform to bumper test shall be completed within two hours of the impactor being removed from the controlled storage area.
The target points selected for the upper legform tests shall lie within the bumper test area as defined in paragraph 3.10.

At the time of first contact, the upper legform impactor centre line shall be vertically midway between the upper bumper reference line and the lower bumper reference line, with a tolerance of +10 mm.
The upper legform impact direction shall be parallel to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle with the upper legform axis vertical at first contact, with a tolerance of ±2°.
The upper legform impactor vertical centre line shall be positioned laterally at the selected impact location with a tolerance of ±10 mm.
The impact velocity of the upper legform impactor striking the bumper shall be 11.1 ± 0.2 m/s.
An approval mark shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under UN R10 (no marking required for systems built into vehicles approved as units).
The ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10.
The ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band the limit shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the limits shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation.
The measured broadband emission values of the ESA representative of its type, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
The measured narrowband emission value of the ESA representative of its type, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The transient conducted emissions of the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 and shall meet the pulse amplitude levels given in Table 1.
For ESAs on 12 V systems, the maximum allowed transient conducted pulse amplitude shall be +75 V for positive pulses and -100 V for negative pulses.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation by the method(s) as described in Annex 9.

The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity for the minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band is as given in Table 2b.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band are given in Table 2a.
An ESA that does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2 or 6.6.2 and with Annexes 5 and 8.
The ESA shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" during the radiated immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.

For pulse 1, the ESA shall meet immunity test level -75 V (12V system) or -450 V (24V system) for 500 pulses with FPSC III for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

For pulse 2a, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +37 V (12V system) or +37 V (24V system) for 500 pulses with FPSC I for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

For pulse 2b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +10 V (12V system) or +20 V (24V system) for 10 pulses with FPSC II for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

For pulse 3a, the ESA shall meet immunity test level -112 V (12V system) or -150 V (24V system) for 1 h with FPSC I for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

For pulse 3b, the ESA shall meet immunity test level +75 V (12V system) or +150 V (24V system) for 1 h with FPSC I for functions related to immunity and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity as specified in Table 3b.

For the 12 V system starting profile (ISO 16750-2, test level II, 10 pulses), an ESA that shall be operational during engine start phases shall reach functional status class B if it performs immunity-related functions and class D if it does not, and any other ESA shall reach class C, as given in Table 3a.
The Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

The immunity of ESA representative of this type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.

The immunity of the ESA to transient disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested per ISO 16750-2 for the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels of Tables 3a and 3b.
The starting profile shall be tested according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.

The starting profile test shall use test level II (10 pulses) for 12 V and 24 V systems, with functional status B for immunity related functions of ESA that shall be operational during engine start phases, C for other ESA, and D for functions not related to immunity related functions, classified per ISO 16750-1.
ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
The ESA broadband electromagnetic radiation shall not exceed E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m in the 75-400 MHz band, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth.
The ESA broadband electromagnetic radiation shall not exceed E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m in the 30-75 MHz band, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth.
The ESA broadband electromagnetic radiation shall not exceed E = 63 dBµV/m in the 400-1,000 MHz band, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth.
The ESA narrowband electromagnetic radiation shall not exceed E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m in the 75-400 MHz band, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth.
The ESA narrowband electromagnetic radiation shall not exceed E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m in the 30-75 MHz band, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth.
The ESA narrowband electromagnetic radiation shall not exceed E = 53 dBµV/m in the 400-1,000 MHz band, measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth.
The ESA immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
The test signal shall be AM modulated with 1 kHz modulation frequency and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
The test signal shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2) with Ton 3 µs and period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range.
The test signal shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3) with Ton 500 µs and period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges.
An ESA exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without a 12V/24V starter motor) shall not be subject to the starting profile.
The ESA shall be subjected to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2, applied to the supply lines and to other connections that may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The ESA shall be subjected to transient test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2, applied to the supply lines and to other connections that may be operationally connected to supply lines.
Any vehicle component that could change shape or position, other than suspension components or active pedestrian protection devices, shall be set to its stowed position during measurements.

If the vehicle is fitted with a badge, mascot or other structure that bends back or retracts under an applied load of maximum 100 N, that load shall be applied before and/or while measurements are taken.
When measurements are performed, the vehicle shall be positioned in its normal ride attitude.
For vehicles with a lower bumper height at the test position >= 425 mm and < 500 mm, the bumper shall meet the requirements of either paragraph 5.1.1 or 5.1.2, at the manufacturer's choice.
For vehicles with a lower bumper height at the test position >= 500 mm, the bumper shall meet the upper legform requirements of paragraph 5.1.2.
For vehicles with a lower bumper height at the test position of less than 425 mm, the bumper shall meet the flexible lower legform requirements of paragraph 5.1.1.
The flexible lower legform impactor used for testing shall be certified pursuant to Annex 6, paragraph 1.
When tested per Annex 5 para 1 (flexible lower legform), the absolute value of maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament elongation at the knee shall not exceed 22 mm.

When tested per Annex 5 paragraph 1 (flexible lower legform), for manufacturer-nominated bumper test widths up to a maximum of 264 mm in total, the absolute value of the tibia bending moment shall not exceed 380 Nm.

When tested per Annex 5 paragraph 1 (flexible lower legform), the absolute value of dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm, except within any manufacturer-nominated relaxation test widths where 380 Nm applies.
When tested per Annex 5 paragraph 1 (flexible lower legform), the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament elongation shall not exceed 13 mm.
The upper legform impactor shall be certified pursuant to Annex 6, paragraph 2.
When tested per Annex 5 para 2 (upper legform to bumper), the instantaneous sum of impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5 kN.
When tested per Annex 5 paragraph 2 (upper legform to bumper), the bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm.

The manufacturer shall provide a detailed description, including photographs and/or drawings, of the vehicle frontal part (interior and exterior) covering structure, dimensions, relevant reference lines and constituent materials, including any active protection system and any system that could change the vehicle front-axle height while driving.
At the time of testing, the test facility and the vehicle or sub-system shall have a relative humidity of 40 % ± 30 % and a stabilized temperature of 20 °C ± 4 °C.
The impact test site shall consist of a flat, smooth and hard surface with a slope not exceeding 1 %.
Either a complete vehicle or a cut-body, adjusted to the specified conditions, shall be used for the test.
The vehicle shall be in its normal ride attitude and shall be either securely mounted on raised supports or at rest on a flat horizontal surface with the parking brake applied.

A cut-body used for testing shall include all parts of the vehicle front structure, all under-bonnet components and all components behind the windscreen that may be involved in a frontal impact with a vulnerable road user, and shall be securely mounted in the normal vehicle ride attitude.

All devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle (e.g. pedestrian impact sensors triggering deployable systems) shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant pedestrian impact test.
The manufacturer shall show that any pedestrian protection devices will act as intended in a pedestrian impact.

For vehicle components that could change shape or position (other than active pedestrian protection devices) and have more than one fixed shape or position, the vehicle shall comply with the requirements with the components in each fixed shape or position.
The compression characteristics of the rubber and neoprene sheets shall conform to Figure 2 and shall be checked using material from the same batch as the sheets used for the impactor flesh and skin.
After removal from storage the impactor shall not be subjected to conditions other than those pertaining in the test area defined in Annex 3, paragraph 1.1.
All impactor components shall be stored for a sufficient period in a controlled storage area at a stabilized temperature of 20 °C ± 4 °C prior to removal for testing.
A horizontal and vertical impact tolerance of ±10 mm shall apply for lower legform testing.
During contact between the impactor and the vehicle, the impactor shall not contact the ground or any object that is not part of the vehicle.
The impact velocity of the impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s, taking the effect of gravity into account when derived from pre-contact measurements.
The tibia bending moments shall not exceed ±15 Nm within an evaluation interval of 30 ms immediately prior to impact.
Offset compensation shall be done with the flexible lower legform impactor in resting position prior to the test/acceleration phase.
Each bumper test shall be completed within two hours of removing the impactor from the controlled storage area.
The selected measuring points shall be in the bumper test area as defined in paragraph 2.14 of the Regulation.

A minimum of three lower legform to bumper tests shall be carried out, one each to the middle and the outer thirds of the bumper test area, at positions judged most likely to cause injury and to different types of structure where they vary.
The positions tested by the laboratories shall be indicated in the test report.
The selected test points shall be a minimum of 84 mm apart, measured horizontally and perpendicular to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.

The impact velocity vector shall be in the horizontal plane and parallel to the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±2° in the horizontal and longitudinal planes at first contact.
The impactor axis shall be perpendicular to the horizontal plane with a roll and pitch angle tolerance of ±2° in the lateral and longitudinal planes.

The bottom of the impactor shall be 75 mm above the ground reference plane at first contact with the bumper, with a ±10 mm tolerance, allowing for gravity during free flight when setting the propulsion height.

The lower legform impactor shall be in free flight at the moment of impact and shall be released at a distance such that test results are not influenced by contact with the propulsion system during rebound.
At first contact the impactor shall have the intended orientation about its vertical axis for correct knee joint operation, with a yaw angle tolerance of ±5°.
For each test the foam flesh shall be two new sheets of 25 mm thick foam type CF-45 or equivalent, cut from the sheet of material used for the dynamic certification test.
The foam and rubber skin shall be folded back towards the rear, with the rubber skin attached via spacers to the rear member so that the sides of the rubber skin are held parallel.

The foam shall be of such a size and shape that an adequate gap is maintained between the foam and components behind the front member, to avoid significant load paths between the foam and these components.
The impactor skin shall be a 1.5 mm thick fibre reinforced rubber sheet.
The mass of the foam and the rubber skin together shall be 0.6 kg ± 0.1 kg, excluding reinforcement and mountings used to attach the rear edges of the skin.
After removal from storage the impactor shall not be subjected to conditions other than those pertaining in the test area.

The test impactor, or at least the foam flesh, shall be stored for at least four hours in a controlled storage area with stabilized humidity of 35 per cent ± 15 per cent and temperature of 20 °C ± 4 °C prior to removal for test.
Each test shall be completed within two hours of removing the impactor from the controlled storage area.
The measuring points selected for the bumper impact tests shall be located within the bumper test area as defined in paragraph 2.14 of the Regulation.

A minimum of three upper legform to bumper tests shall be carried out, one each to the middle third and the outer thirds of the bumper test area, at positions judged most likely to cause injury and on different structure types where they vary.
The positions tested by the laboratories shall be indicated in the test report.
The selected upper legform measuring points shall be a minimum of 84 mm apart, measured horizontally and perpendicular to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.
At first contact the impactor centre line shall be vertically midway between the upper and lower bumper reference lines with a ±10 mm tolerance.
At first contact the impactor vertical centre line shall be positioned laterally at the selected impact location with a tolerance of ±10 mm.
The direction of impact of the upper legform shall be parallel to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, with the upper legform axis vertical at first contact, within a tolerance of ±2°.
The impact velocity of the upper legform impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.
Every lamp of an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the other required markings.
All markings on the lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval marking shall have a dimension "a" of at least 5 mm.
The approval marking shall include the approval mark, a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which granted approval.
The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number of the approval number, placed close to the approval mark.
The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamp function(s) as prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
Lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately shall be marked with a horizontal arrow showing the position in which the lamp is to be mounted.
The mounting arrow on direction indicators of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12 shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
The mounting arrow on direction indicators of categories 5 and 6 and combined parking lamps shall be directed towards the front of the vehicle.
Direction indicators of category 6 shall show an indication "R" or "L" on the lamp indicating the right or left side of the vehicle.
The additional letter "D" shall be marked to the right of the function symbol on lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps.
The additional letter "Y" shall be marked to the right of the function symbol on lamps used as part of an interdependent lamp system.
Light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
The approval mark on the module and on the lamp shall be from the same applicant.
The lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the light source module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5.(a)(ii).
Lamps with reduced light distribution shall be marked with a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
Lamps approved for LED substitute light source(s) shall also bear a marking indicating the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).
Lamps with replaceable light sources shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.

Lamps with an electronic light source control gear, a variable luminous intensity control, a secondary operating mode, or non-replaceable light sources shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (6 V, 12 V or 24 V) or the voltage range.
The lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii) in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

The light source module and the lamp shall both have marks from the same applicant, where the approval mark on the light source module does not have to be the same as the one on the lamp in which the module is used, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

The specific identification code of the module shall comprise the starting letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

Where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used and several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of the module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.

An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control that is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part of the lamp that is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.

The approval marking and, if any, the category or categories of the prescribed LED substitute light source(s) shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood, boot lid or a door is opened.
The approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable outer lens and the main body of the device.
Where an outer lens is used for several devices bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5.(b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the component.
The markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3.(a), 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. and 3.3.3.6. need not fulfil the requirements of paragraph 3.3.4.2.
A single approval mark on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall be visible after their installation.
No part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.
The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations.
Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4 and 5 of the Regulation.

The lamp shall meet the requirements of sections 5 and 6 (and referenced Annexes) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86 in force at the time of application, as pertinent to the lamp and vehicle category, where verification at type approval is feasible.

The lamps shall be designed and constructed so that in normal conditions of use, notwithstanding vibrations, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.
A front position lamp that incorporates infrared radiation generator(s) shall meet its photometric and colour requirements both with and without operation of the infrared radiation generator(s).

The enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) of a lamp, where the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of the lamp incorporates only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant, shall not exceed 100 cm2 in the direction of the reference axis.

The internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) shall fulfill all requirements for the specific function of this Regulation when incorporating only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant.

The internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) shall incorporate only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer, irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3., when incorporating only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant.

The logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) shall not be required to be symmetrical by itself, notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, when the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant.
In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that failure of any one causes all to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.

On failure of any one light source in a single lamp with more than one light source, either the light intensity shall still comply with the minimum intensity of the standard light distribution table in Annex 3 (with maximum intensities not exceeded when all sources are lit), or a tell-tale failure signal shall be produced.
Where the tell-tale failure option is used, a note in the communication form shall state that the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.

For direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12, a tell-tale activation signal shall be produced when any one light source has failed, or (for a lamp designed for two light sources only) when the intensity in the reference axis falls below 50 per cent of the required minimum, or when the intensity falls below the required minimum in the directions H=0°/V=0°, H=20° outwards/V=+5° or H=10° inwards/V=0°.

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128 (with no restriction on use made at application), and/or light source module(s), and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
The lamp design shall be such that the replaceable light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.

The light source holder shall conform to the characteristics in IEC Publication 60061, using the holder data sheet relevant to the prescribed light source category (and to the LED substitute category where prescribed).
Light signalling devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances that cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that the light source module(s) can only be fitted in the designated and correct position.

The design of the light source module(s) shall be such that regardless of the use of tool(s), the light source module(s) is not interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source and/or any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.
The design of the light source module(s) shall be such that the light source module(s) can only be removed with the use of tool(s) in case of replaceable light source module(s).
The design of the light source module(s) shall be such that the light source module(s) is tamperproof in case of replaceable light source module(s).

When the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, in case of replaceable light source module(s), the device shall meet the photometric requirements.
For replaceable UN approved light sources, all photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be made using standard light sources as specified in R.E.5.

For replaceable UN approved light source(s) controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control, the standard light source(s) shall have a luminous flux that deviates by no more than 5 per cent from the reference/objective luminous flux when test voltage is applied.
For a lamp with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), all measurements shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.

For a lamp (function) using light sources subject to more than one of the conditions in paragraph 4.8, the photometric measurements shall be made separately for each applicable condition and the separate results shall be added together.
During photometric measurements of the lamp, stray reflections shall be avoided by appropriate masking.

Where the lamp is also to be approved with LED substitute light source(s) at the applicant's discretion, all photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be repeated using the prescribed LED substitute light source(s).
Unless otherwise specified, luminous intensities of the lamp shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.
When measurement results are challenged, the measurement distance shall be such that the inverse square law of distance is applicable.
When measurement results are challenged, the measuring equipment shall be such that the angular aperture of the receiver viewed from the reference centre of the light is between 10' and 1 degree.
The intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation shall be deemed satisfied if met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from that direction.

The limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the light-signalling lamp shall be determined (for category 5 and 6 direction indicators, the limits of the light emitting surface shall be determined).
Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp during testing shall be 6.75 V (6 V systems), 13.5 V (12 V systems) or 28 V (24 V systems).

For replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light sources shall be operated at the reference/objective luminous flux, or alternatively at a different luminous flux with proportional correction of the measured luminous intensities.

Lamps with multiple replaceable UN approved light sources shall be operated at a voltage or current setting such that actual luminous fluxes of the light sources do not deviate by more than 5 per cent from their average, and measured intensities shall be corrected proportionally for the difference between average and reference/objective luminous flux.

Alternatively, such lamps may be tested using one light source in each lamp holder position operating at the reference/objective luminous flux, summing the measured luminous intensities for each direction.

The identification of the electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control, if applicable, and/or the applied voltage including tolerances shall be noted in the communication form in Annex 1.
In no direction where the lamp is visible shall the luminous intensity exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
On the reference axis (HV), the luminous intensity of each of the two samples shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

Outside the reference axis, the luminous intensity shall be not less than the minimum specified in the function table multiplied by the percentage given in the pertinent light distribution figure in Annex 3, or not less than the intensity value specified in that figure, for each direction.
The provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed.
Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, the luminous intensity shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If the applicant requests an additional test, the maximum intensity in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard horizontally and -2.5° to +5° vertically shall be not more than 2.5·10^-1 cd (may take vehicle body influence into account).

An assembly of two independent lamps marked "D" with the same function deemed a single lamp shall comply with the maximum intensity requirement when all lamps are lit together and the minimum intensity requirement if either lamp has failed.
An interdependent lamp system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the limits specified in the sub-paragraphs of 4.8.3.4.

The variable intensity control shall not generate signals causing luminous intensities exceeding the steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5 for the specific lamp: under night-time conditions for systems depending only on day/night conditions, otherwise under standard conditions.

For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics shall be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with the relevant sub-paragraphs of 4.8.

The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in Annex 3, using the test procedure of paragraph 4.8, and no sharp variation of colour shall be observed outside this field.
For lamps (functions) using different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics shall be checked for each light source technology separately per paragraphs 4.8.1 and 4.8.2.
A front position lamp marked "D" shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 70 cd (7.0E1 cd).
The front position lamp (category A, MA) shall emit a luminous intensity of at least 4 cd (4.0E0 cd) in the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I.
The front position lamp (category A, MA) used as a single lamp shall not exceed a maximum luminous intensity of 140 cd (1.40E2 cd).
The front position lamp shall emit at least 0.05 cd (5E-2 cd) within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1.
The light emitted by each of the two supplied samples of the front position lamp shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 3.
The front position lamp shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility as specified in Table 3 (0.05 cd).
The colour of the light emitted by the front position lamp shall be white; a lamp identified by symbol MA may be amber.

A category 1 direction indicator shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 175 cd and a maximum of 1200 cd as a single lamp (600 cd when marked "D"), standard light distribution Figure A3-I, geometric visibility per Table A2-1 with minimum 0.3 cd.

A category 1a direction indicator shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 250 cd and a maximum of 1200 cd as a single lamp (600 cd when marked "D"), standard light distribution Figure A3-I, geometric visibility per Table A2-1 with minimum 0.3 cd.

A category 1b direction indicator shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 400 cd and a maximum of 1200 cd as a single lamp (600 cd when marked "D"), standard light distribution Figure A3-I, geometric visibility per Table A2-1 with minimum 0.7 cd.
For direction indicators of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12, the minimum luminous intensities of Table 8 shall be fulfilled in the reference axis.
For direction indicators of categories 5 and 6, the minimum luminous intensities of Table 8 shall be fulfilled in direction A according to Annex 2.
The light emitted by each of the two samples of a direction indicator lamp supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 8.
The direction indicator lamp shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility specified in Table 8.
For measurements taken in flashing mode, the reported luminous intensity shall be the maximum intensity.
In other cases the voltage required in paragraph 4.8 shall be switched with a rise time and fall time shorter than 0.01 s and no overshoot allowed.
The intensities of the direction indicator lamp shall in general be measured with the light source(s) continuously alight.

Where measurement is taken in flashing mode (permitted due to e.g. LED construction or overheating precautions), switching shall be at f = 1.5 ± 0.5 Hz with pulse width greater than 0.3 s measured at 95 per cent peak light intensity.
Compliance with the sequential activation conditions shall be verified in flashing mode.

The distance between two adjacent or tangential distinct parts of the light emitting surface of a sequential direction indicator shall not exceed 50 mm, measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
The interruptions between distinct parts of the light emitting surface of a sequential direction indicator shall not be used for any other lighting or light signalling functions.

The interruptions between distinct parts of the light emitting surface of a sequential direction indicator shall not create any overlap in the vertical axis between the different parts, from inboard towards outboard of the vehicle.

The orthogonal projection of the light emitting surfaces of the sequential direction indicator in the direction of the reference axis shall be circumscribed by a rectangle with its longer sides parallel to the H-plane and a horizontal to vertical side ratio of not less than 1.7.
The sequence of activation of the light sources shall produce a signal that proceeds in a uniform progressive manner from inboard towards the outboard edge of the light emitting surface.
The sequential signal shall be one signal with no interruption and no vertical oscillations (not more than one change of direction along the vertical axis).
The variation of the sequential flash shall finish no more than 200 ms after the beginning of the ON cycle.
Where a direction indicator flash is produced by sequential activation of light sources, each light source shall remain lit after its activation until the end of the ON cycle.
The colour of light emitted by the direction indicator lamp shall be amber.

A category SM1 side marker lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4.0 cd in the axis of reference, a minimum of 0.6 cd within the standard light distribution (Figure A3-VII), a maximum of 25 cd, and a minimum of 0.6 cd within the angles of geometric visibility (Table A2-3).

A category SM2 side marker lamp shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 0.6 cd in the axis of reference, a minimum of 0.6 cd within the standard light distribution (Figure A3-VIII), a maximum of 25 cd, and a minimum of 0.6 cd within the angles of geometric visibility (Table A2-3).
For a red side marker lamp, the maximum luminous intensity in the angular field from 60° to 90° horizontally and ±20° vertically towards the front of the vehicle shall be limited to 2.5·10^-1 cd.
The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the side marker lamp shall meet the luminous intensity requirements of Table 9.
The side marker lamp shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility given in Table 9 (0.6 cd for SM1 and SM2).
For SM1 and SM2 side marker lamps, photometric verification may be limited to checking five points selected by the Type Approval Authority.
Lamps shall be manufactured to conform to the type approved under UN R148, and compliance with the requirements of paragraph 5 shall be verified.
For the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values shall correspond to the values shown in Table 12.

Measured minimum luminous intensity values in CoP shall be at least the 20 per cent equivalents (e.g. 7·10-1 cd required -> 5·10-1 cd; 6·10-1 -> 4·10-1; 3·10-1 -> 2·10-1; 7·10-2 -> 5·10-2; 5·10-2 -> 3·10-2), or the 30 per cent equivalents (3·10-1, 2·10-1, 1·10-1, 3·10-2, 2·10-2 cd respectively) where the 30 per cent tolerance applies.
No measured photometric value of a production lamp shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in UN R148.

Front direction indicator lamps (categories 1, 1a, 1b) shall have minimum angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 80° outboard horizontally (20° inboard / 80° outboard reduced) and 15° above / 15° below vertically (15° above / 5° below reduced).

Front/rear direction indicator lamps (categories 11, 11a, 11b, 11c, 12) shall have minimum angles of geometric visibility of 20° inboard / 80° outboard horizontally and 15° above / 15° below vertically (15° above / 5° below reduced).
The reduced horizontal angles of Table A2-1 shall be used only below the H-plane and only for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm.
the reduced vertical angles apply to lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height below 750 mm.
Side direction indicator lamps (category 5) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 5° / 55° (A/B) and vertical angles of 15° above / 15° below (15° above / 5° below reduced).
For side marker lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, the minimum downward vertical angle of geometric visibility may be reduced to 5°.

Side marker lamps (SM1) shall have minimum angles of geometric visibility of 45° / 45° horizontally and 10° above / 10° below vertically; SM2 shall have 30° / 30° horizontally and 10° above / 10° below vertically.

Photometric intensity values in the Annex 3 figures shall be taken as minimum intensities, as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, relative to the reference axis (H = 0°, V = 0°) through the centre of reference, mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.

Within the field of light distribution shown as a grid, the light pattern shall be substantially uniform, i.e. the intensity in each direction shall meet at least the lowest minimum value shown on the grid lines surrounding that direction as a percentage.
The photometric performance of mass-produced lamps shall be deemed conforming when any lamp chosen at random is tested for photometric performance in accordance with paragraph 4.8 of the Regulation.
Direction indicator lamps shall be operated in flashing mode (f = 1.5 Hz, duty factor 50 per cent) during the photometric measurements.

For lamps using non-incandescent light source technology (other than reversing and manoeuvring lamps), the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
Direction indicator lamps of Categories 1, 2, 11, 12 shall comply with the luminous intensity requirements 0.2 seconds after switch ON, measured at reference coordinate HV.
Direction indicator lamps of Categories 5, 6 shall comply with the luminous intensity requirements 0.2 seconds after switch ON, measured at reference coordinate H5, V0.
Side marker lamps shall comply with the luminous intensity requirements 4 seconds after switch ON, measured at reference coordinate HV.

The luminous intensity distribution of the lamp shall, in addition to the Annex 8 paragraph 1 checks, comply at the point in time after switch ON listed in Table A8-1 for the relevant lamp function, depending on light source technology.
A lamp (function) using LED technology only shall be deemed to comply with the intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to Annex 8 paragraph 1.2 are compliant.

In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the minimum intensity requirements of the lamp (function) shall be tested and comply at all points in time, starting at the point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.

The floor line of the vehicle (incl. bumper) shall be determined by positioning a cone with vertical axis and 30° half angle in contact with the external surface of the laden vehicle as low as possible, ignoring jacking points, exhaust pipes and wheels, taking the bumper into consideration at both vehicle ends, using the lower contact point where two or more occur simultaneously.

The vehicle shall be tested laden to the maximum permitted technical mass, and vehicles with hydropneumatic, hydraulic or pneumatic suspension or automatic load levelling shall be tested in the most adverse normal running condition specified by the manufacturer.

The external surface of the vehicle (including the bumper fascia and integrated components) shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by or brushing against it in a collision.
The external surface of the vehicle (including the bumper module) shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.

For parts of the external surface protruding less than 5 mm, which are exempt from the 2.5 mm minimum radius of curvature, the outward facing angles shall be blunted, except where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.
No protruding part of the external surface of the bumper module shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm.
Protruding parts of the external surface made of a material of hardness not exceeding 60 Shore A may have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm.
The hardness measurement shall be taken with the component as installed on the vehicle; where Shore A measurement is impossible, comparable measurements shall be used for evaluation.

Added ornaments projecting more than 10 mm from their support shall retract, become detached or bend over under a force of 10 daN exerted at their most salient point in any direction in a plane approximately parallel to the mounting surface.
After the ornaments are retracted, detached or bent over, the remaining projections shall not project more than 10 mm and shall satisfy paragraph 5.2.
The 10 daN force shall be applied using a flat-ended ram of not more than 50 mm diameter, or an equivalent method where this is not possible.
Protective strips or shielding on the external surface shall be firmly secured to the vehicle.
For gaps between 40 mm and 25 mm, the radii of curvature shall be 1 mm or more.

The 2.5 mm radius requirement of 5.4 does not apply to gaps between fixed or movable elements (including air intake/outlet and radiator grilles) provided the distance between consecutive elements does not exceed 40 mm and the grilles and gaps have a functional purpose.
The distance between two consecutive elements of grilles and gaps shall be determined according to the method described in paragraph 4 of Annex 3.
Where the distance between two consecutive elements is equal to or less than 25 mm, the radii of curvature of the external faces of the elements shall not be less than 0.5 mm.
The junction of the front with the side faces of each element forming a grille or gap shall be blunted.

The ends of the bumper shall be turned in towards the external surface to minimize the risk of fouling; this is satisfied if the bumper is recessed or integrated within the bodywork, or the bumper end is turned in so it cannot be contacted by a 100 mm sphere and the gap between the bumper end and surrounding bodywork does not exceed 20 mm.

Where the bumper line corresponding to the outline contour of the car vertical projection is on a rigid surface, that surface shall have a minimum radius of curvature of 2.5 mm at all points other than those lying from the contour line to 20 mm inward within the zone defined by the 15° vertical planes.

Where the bumper line corresponding to the outline contour of the car vertical projection is on a rigid surface, that surface shall have a minimum radius of curvature of 5 mm at all points from the contour line to 20 mm inward, within the zone between tangential points of two vertical planes each at 15° to the longitudinal plane of symmetry.
Parts on or of the bumper or bumper insets projecting less than 5 mm are exempt from 6.5.2, but their outward-facing angles shall be blunted unless the parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.
The bumper cover shall comply with the general requirements of paragraph 5 of UN R26, although the 6.5.2 requirement does not apply to it.
The projection of the charge port flap/cover (fuel filler cap equivalent) integrated in the bumper shall not exceed 30 mm.
Any air intake and outlet flaps in the bumper/grill shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4 in all positions of use.
Folds in the fascia/body panels with a radius of curvature of less than 2.5 mm shall have a radius of curvature not less than one-tenth of the projection height H, measured per Annex 3 paragraph 1.

Supporting brackets for registration plates provided by the vehicle manufacturer (the license plate holder of the bumper) that are contactable by a 100 mm diameter sphere when a registration plate is fitted per the manufacturer's recommendation shall comply with the requirements of paragraph 5.4 of UN R26.

The radio receiving/transmitting aerial (keyless-entry aerial) shall be fitted so that, if its unattached end is less than 2 m from the road surface in any position of use specified by the aerial manufacturer, it is inside the zone bounded by vertical planes 10 cm inside the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

The aerial shall be fitted to the vehicle, and if necessary its unattached end restricted, so that no part of the aerial protrudes beyond the extreme outer edge of the vehicle as defined in paragraph 2.7.
The unattached ends of aerials shall be fitted with fixed cappings having radii of curvature of not less than 2.5 mm (shafts may have radii less than 2.5 mm).
The bases of aerials shall not project more than 40 mm when determined according to the procedure of paragraph 2 of Annex 3.

Where the base of an aerial cannot be identified due to absence of a flexible shaft or part, the aerial shall, after a horizontal force of not more than 50 daN is applied forward and rearward by a flat-ended ram of not more than 50 mm diameter at the most salient part, either (a) bend towards the support and not project more than 40 mm, or (b) break off leaving a remaining part with no sharp or dangerous part contactable by the 100 mm sphere and not projecting more than 40 mm.

For aerials located behind the vertical transversal plane through the driver's R point, the maximum projection including housing shall not exceed 70 mm determined per paragraph 2 of Annex 3; if projecting more than 70 mm, paragraph 6.17.4.1 shall apply with a 70 mm limit instead of 40 mm.

Radio receiving or transmitting aerials approved as separate technical units shall be accompanied by assembly instructions containing sufficient information to mount them in compliance with paragraphs 5 and 6, including indicating positions of use for telescopic aerials.
The vehicle (separate technical unit) approved under UN R26 shall be manufactured to conform to the approved type by meeting the requirements of paragraphs 5 and 6.
The approval holder shall ensure the existence of procedures for the effective control of the quality of products.
The approval holder shall have access to the control equipment necessary for checking conformity to each approved type.
The approval holder shall ensure that test result data are recorded and related documents remain available for a period determined with the Type Approval Authority.
The approval holder shall analyze the results of each type of test to verify and ensure the stability of product characteristics, allowing for variation of industrial production.
The approval holder shall ensure that for each type of product at least the tests prescribed in Annex 3 to UN R26 are carried out.

The height H of a projection on the body panel (fascia) shall be determined graphically by reference to the circumference of a 165 mm diameter circle internally tangential to the external outline of the external surface at the section to be checked.

H shall be taken as the maximum distance, measured along a straight line passing through the centre of the 165 mm diameter circle, between the circle circumference and the external contour of the projection.

Where a 100 mm diameter circle cannot contact part of the external outline of the external surface at the section considered, the surface outline in that area shall be assumed to be the circumference of the 100 mm circle between its tangent points with the external outline.
The manufacturer shall provide drawings of the necessary sections through the external surface to allow the height of the projections to be measured.
The projection dimension of a component mounted on a convex surface may be determined directly or by reference to a drawing of an appropriate section of the component in its installed condition.

Where the projection of a component mounted on a non-convex surface cannot be determined by simple measurement, it shall be determined as the maximum variation of the distance of the centre of a 100 mm diameter sphere from the nominal line of the panel while the sphere is moved over, and kept in constant contact with, the component.
The projection from the external surface of the headlamp shall be measured horizontally from the point of contact of a 100 mm diameter sphere.

The dimension of a gap or space between grille elements shall be determined as the distance between two planes passing through the sphere contact points and perpendicular to the line joining those contact points.
After each low-speed impact test, the lighting and signalling devices (including those integrated in the front bumper module) shall continue to operate correctly and remain visible.
After each low-speed impact test, the vehicle's bonnet (hood), boot lid (trunk lid) and doors shall be operable in the normal manner.
the side doors shall not open under the effect of the impact.

After each low-speed impact test, the vehicle's fuel and cooling systems shall have neither leaks nor constricted fluid passages preventing normal functioning, and their sealing devices and caps shall be operable in the normal manner.
After the impact test, the vehicle's exhaust system shall not suffer any damage or displacement that would prevent its normal function.

After the impact test, the vehicle's propulsion, suspension (including tyres), steering and braking systems shall remain in adjustment and shall operate in a normal manner, except for sensors, cameras, radar devices etc. that are part of driver assist systems.
Where driver-assist sensors, cameras or radar devices are damaged, disoriented or broken by the Annex 3 impact, the basic braking and steering performance of the vehicle shall remain intact.

The vehicle shall be placed on a horizontal and level rigid smooth surface in a test area large enough to accommodate the impactor propulsion system, the after-impact displacement of the vehicle, and the test equipment.
The vehicle shall be at rest during the impact test.
The front wheels shall be in the straight-ahead position during the impact test.
The tyres shall be inflated to the pressure recommended by the vehicle manufacturer during the impact test.
The brakes shall be disengaged and the transmission control shall be in the neutral position during the impact test.

Vehicles equipped with hydro-pneumatic, hydraulic or pneumatic suspension or a device for automatic levelling according to load shall be tested in the normal running conditions specified by the manufacturer.
The impactor shall be of rigid construction, with the impact contour made of hardened steel.
The impacting surface of the impactor shall conform to the diagram in the figure.
The effective mass of the impactor shall be equal to the mass corresponding to the unladen weight of the vehicle to be tested.
With plane A of the impactor vertical, the reference line of the impactor shall be horizontal.
In both vehicle-loading conditions, the protective device between the corners (as defined in paragraph 3.1.5) shall be intersected by the horizontal plane passing through the reference line.
The first contact of the impactor with the vehicle shall be by the impact contour on the protective device (front bumper).
The impactor reference height shall be 445 mm.
If the impactor is secured to a carriage (moving barrier) by a restraining element, the restraining element shall be rigid and incapable of being deformed by the impact.
The carriage shall at the moment of impact be capable of moving freely and no longer be subject to the action of the propelling device.
The distance between the pendulum pivot and the centre of percussion shall be at least 3.3 m.
The reference line shall coincide with the centre of percussion of the pendulum.
Plane A of the pendulum shall remain parallel with its axis of rotation throughout the test.
For a parallelogram-suspended pendulum, the trajectory described by any point on the reference line shall be constant with a radius of at least 3.3 m.

The test shall consist of two impacts on the front surface and two impacts on the rear surface of the vehicle; on each surface one impact shall be made at unladen weight (3.1.3) and one at laden test weight (3.1.4).
During the impacts, the extremities of the impactor shall not pass outside a zone defined by two planes parallel to the longitudinal median plane and passing through the vehicle corners.
For the second impact on each of the front and rear surfaces, the median plane of the impactor shall be at least 300 mm from the first impact.
The impactor shall be placed so that plane A is vertical and the reference line is horizontal at the reference height of 445 mm.

The vehicle shall be aligned so that a point between the vehicle corners touches, but does not move, the impactor, with the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle perpendicular to plane A of the impactor.

The corner impact test shall consist of an impact at one front corner and one rear corner with the vehicle at unladen weight (3.1.3), and an impact at the other front corner and other rear corner with the vehicle at the weight given in 3.1.4.
The impactor shall be placed so that plane A is vertical and the reference line is horizontal at the reference height of 445 mm.
Plane A of the impactor shall make an angle of 60 ± 5° with the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.
The point of first contact shall be in the vertical median plane of the impactor within a tolerance of ± 25 mm.
The vehicle shall be aligned so that a corner of the vehicle touches the impactor without moving it.
If the protective device includes self-restoring materials, the permitted recovery time between tests shall be as stated by the manufacturer.
The instrument used to record the impact speed shall be accurate to within one per cent.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall prevent the lamps from being inadvertently maladjusted under normal conditions of use and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected.
Any specific fitting instructions laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with when installing the light-signalling devices.
The reference axis of each light-signalling device, when fitted to the vehicle, shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.

The reference axis shall be perpendicular to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle for side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, and parallel to that plane for all other signalling devices, with a tolerance of ±3° in each direction.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2., and with any AFS in its neutral state.

Lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane, judged on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface.
Lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane, except with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
Lamps fitted as a pair on the vehicle shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics, except for a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.

Where lamps incorporate a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo shall be fitted on the front of the vehicle, and logos other than vehicle or body manufacturer logos shall not be used.
On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the installation requirements for the lamps shall be satisfied as far as possible.

Lamps in the bumper that are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated shall fulfil all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements.
The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which it is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

When a front position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with other function(s) that can be switched ON together with it, the colour requirements of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled with the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front position lamp switched ON.

For a single lamp as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1(a) whose apparent surface is composed of two or more distinct parts, either the total area of the projection of the distinct parts in the direction of the reference axis, on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis, shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the apparent surface, or the 75 mm facing-edge distance criterion of 5.7.2.1(b) shall be met; this does not apply to a single retro-reflector.

For a single lamp as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1(a) whose apparent surface is composed of two or more distinct parts, where the 60 per cent projected-area criterion of 5.7.2.1(a) is not met, the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 75 mm, measured perpendicularly to the reference axis; this does not apply to a single retro-reflector.

For a single lamp as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1(b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro-reflectors, either the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projections, or the 75 mm facing-edge distance criterion of 5.7.2.2(b) shall be met.

For a single lamp as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1(b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro-reflectors, where the 60 per cent projection criterion of 5.7.2.2(a) is not met, the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 75 mm, measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
Single lamps as defined in 2.4.11.1(d) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.
The illumination of a band or strip lamp surface shall be provided by not less than two light sources placed as close as possible to the ends.

Two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be placed symmetrically about the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, extend on both sides to within at least 0.4 m of the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, and be not less than 0.8 m long.

Where the light-emitting surface of a band or strip lamp is constituted by a number of juxtaposed elements, the individual light-emitting surfaces, when projected on a transverse plane, shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.
White light emitted by a lamp fitted on the front of the vehicle shall not be visible from the rear of the vehicle.
The maximum height above the ground of a lamp shall be measured from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
For the purpose of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the height of a lamp above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.

The position of a lamp as regards width shall be determined from the edge of the apparent surface furthest from the median longitudinal plane when referred to overall width, and from the inner edges of the apparent surface when referred to the distance between lamps.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
Direction-indicator lamps, the vehicle-hazard warning signal, amber side-marker lamps complying with 6.18.7 and the emergency stop signal shall be flashing lamps.

Any variation of a lamp's photometric characteristics (due to ambient light, other lamps being switched ON/OFF, or use for another lighting function) shall comply with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

The photometric characteristics of a direction indicator lamp of category 1, 1a, 1b, 2a or 2b may be varied during a flash by sequential activation of light sources only as specified in paragraph 5.6 of UN Regulation No. 6 or 5.6.11 of UN Regulation No. [LSD]; this does not apply to categories 2a and 2b operated as emergency stop signal per 6.23.1.

No red lamp integrated in the front bumper module (other than a red rearmost side-marker lamp) shall have its apparent surface directly visible to an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane 25 m in front of the vehicle.

In case of doubt, the requirement of 5.10.4 shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.
In an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
The concealment of lamps shall be prohibited, with the exception of main-beam headlamps, dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps, which may be concealed when they are not in use.
A direction-indicator lamp integrated in the bumper shall emit amber light.
A front position lamp integrated in the bumper shall emit white light.
A side-marker lamp integrated in the bumper shall emit amber light.
If any lamp is installed on movable components, the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18, 5.19 and 5.20 shall be fulfilled.

For direction indicator lamps in an interdependent system partly on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant shall meet all position, geometric visibility, photometric and colorimetric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component(s), unless additional lamps are switched ON in a fixed open position and satisfy all position, photometric and colorimetric requirements.

Where a complete interdependent lamp system is mounted on the moving component(s), the requirements of 5.18.1 shall be satisfied, and any additional lamps switched ON in a fixed open position shall meet all position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps on the movable component.

Where an interdependent lamp system is partly on the fixed and partly on a movable component (other than direction indicators), the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant shall meet all position, outwards geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
Devices installed on movable components shall not cause undue discomfort to road users when the movable components are in a position other than a normal position of use.
A lamp installed on a movable component in the normal position(s) of use shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with this Regulation.

Additional lamps satisfying all position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the lamp is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

A remark in the communication form (item 10.1 of Annex 1) shall inform other Administrations that more than 50 per cent of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis can be hidden by the movable components.
A lamp, other than a retro-reflector, shall be operable by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse, otherwise it is deemed not present even if it bears an approval mark.
The vehicle manufacturer shall provide with the vehicle a detailed description of the light source replacement procedure.
Where a light source module includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source per UN R37, that light source shall be replaceable as required in 5.23.

For M and N category vehicles the applicant shall demonstrate to the Technical Service that the electric power supply conditions for the devices indicated in 2.5.1, 2.5.2, 2.5.4, 2.5.6 and 2.5.7 comply with the provisions of 5.27.1 and 5.27.2 when the vehicle electrical system is in a constant voltage operating condition.

The voltage supplied at the terminals of devices tested with a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, a secondary operating mode or an applicant-requested voltage shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as approved.

In all cases not covered by 5.27.1, the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 V systems), 13.5 V (12 V systems) or 28 V (24 V systems) by more than 3 per cent.

The voltage provisions of 5.27.1 and 5.27.2 shall not apply to devices including an electronic light source control gear, a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light sources approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity, except obstacles already present when the lamp was type-approved.
If geometric visibility measurements are taken closer to the lamp than infinity, the direction of observation shall be shifted parallel to achieve the same accuracy.

If any part of the apparent surface of the installed lamp is hidden by other vehicle parts, proof shall be furnished that the non-hidden part still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
