Where the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal is reduced to 5° (lamp less than 750 mm above the ground, measured per 5.8.1), the photometric measurement field of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5° below the horizontal.
For an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
All lamps (devices) installed on the vehicle shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations specified in paragraph 6.
A light-signalling lamp incorporating a manufacturer logo shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.

Lamps installed on a vehicle and approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128 shall be fitted only with light sources approved according to those categories, except that this requirement does not concern light source modules, LED modules and non-replaceable light sources unless they are required to be approved by the applicable Regulation.

Direction-indicator lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 6, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

Front direction-indicator lamps shall be of category 1, 1a or 1b where the distance between the edge of the apparent surface of the lamp and that of the dipped-beam headlamp and/or front fog lamp, if there is one, is at least 40 mm.

Front direction-indicator lamps shall be of category 1a or 1b where the distance between the edge of the apparent surface of the lamp and that of the dipped-beam headlamp and/or front fog lamp, if there is one, is greater than 20 mm and less than 40 mm.

Front direction-indicator lamps shall be of category 1b where the distance between the edge of the apparent surface of the lamp and that of the dipped-beam headlamp and/or front fog lamp, if there is one, is less than or equal to 20 mm.
Two side direction-indicator lamps of category 5 (or category 6 as a permitted replacement) shall be fitted as the minimum requirement on M1 vehicles.

Where an AFS is fitted, the distance used for choosing the front direction-indicator category shall be the distance between the front direction-indicator lamp and the closest lighting unit, in its closest position, contributing to or performing a passing-beam mode.

The distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes shall not be less than 600 mm, which may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall vehicle width is less than 1,300 mm.

The edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the direction-indicator lamp farthest from the median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
The light-emitting surface of side direction-indicator lamps of category 5 or 6 shall be not less than 350 mm above the ground for M1 and N1 vehicles, measured from the lowest point.
The light-emitting surface of side direction-indicator lamps of category 5 or 6 shall be not more than 1,500 mm above the ground, measured from the highest point.
The height of direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b, measured in accordance with paragraph 5.8, shall be not less than 350 mm and not more than 1,500 mm.

Where the vehicle structure does not permit the normal upper height limits and optional rear lamps are not installed, the upper height limit of direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b may be increased to 2,100 mm.

Where the vehicle structure does not permit the normal upper height limits and optional rear lamps are not installed, the upper height limit of side direction-indicator lamps of categories 5 and 6 may be increased to 2,300 mm.

For M1 vehicles, the distance between the light-emitting surface of the side direction-indicator lamp (categories 5 and 6) and the transverse plane marking the forward boundary of the vehicle's overall length shall not exceed 2,500 mm.
Optional category 5 side direction-indicator lamps shall be fitted spaced evenly along the length of the vehicle.

The distance between the light-emitting surface of a side direction-indicator lamp (category 5 or 6) and the transverse plane marking the forward boundary of the vehicle's overall length shall not exceed 1,800 mm, or 2,500 mm for M1 and N1 category vehicles.
For direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b mounted below 750 mm, the inward visibility angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
Where a direction-indicator lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured per 5.8.1), the downward visibility angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
For direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b mounted below 750 mm, the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
To be considered visible, the lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres, except for side direction-indicators of categories 5 and 6.
Where a lamp under the alternative M1 arrangement is mounted below 750 mm, the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

Where the alternative arrangement for M1 and N1 category vehicles is chosen, front direction-indicator lamps and side-marker lamps shall have a vertical geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal, the downward angle being reducible to 5° where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm.
Direction-indicator lamps shall be oriented according to the manufacturer's installation specifications, if any.
A direction indicator capable of being activated in different modes (static or sequential) shall not switch between both modes once activated.
All direction-indicator lamps on one side of the vehicle shall be switched ON and OFF automatically as defined by applicable UN Regulations and/or by means of one control and shall flash in phase.
Direction-indicator lamps shall switch ON independently of the other lamps.

On M1 and N1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length with an arrangement complying with paragraph 6.5.5.2, the amber side-marker lamps, when mounted, shall flash at the same frequency and in phase with the direction-indicator lamps.
An operating tell-tale shall be provided for direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a and 2b.
If entirely auditory, the tell-tale shall be clearly audible and shall show a marked change of frequency, at least in the event of malfunction of any of these direction-indicator lamps.

If visual, the tell-tale shall be a flashing light which, at least in the event of malfunction of any of these direction-indicator lamps, is either extinguished, remains alight without flashing, or shows a marked change of frequency.
it may be visual, auditory or both.
In the event of failure, other than short-circuit, of one direction-indicator lamp, the others shall continue to flash, though the frequency may differ from that prescribed.
Operation of the light-signal control shall be followed within not more than one second by emission of light and within not more than 1.5 seconds by its first extinction.
The direction-indicator light shall be a flashing light flashing 90 ± 30 times per minute.

The vehicle shall be fitted with two front position lamps, type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7 or the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

The point on the apparent surface of the front position lamp in the direction of the reference axis farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
The front position lamp shall be mounted above the ground at a height of not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the bodywork shape makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm).

Where the front position lamp and another lamp are reciprocally incorporated, the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the other lamp shall be used to verify compliance with the positioning requirements of 6.9.4.1 to 6.9.4.3.
The front position lamp shall have a horizontal geometric visibility angle of 45° inwards and 80° outwards.
The front position lamp shall have a vertical geometric visibility angle of 15° above and below the horizontal.
Where the front position lamp is mounted below 750 mm, the downward vertical angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
Where the front position lamp is mounted below 750 mm, the inward horizontal angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

As an alternative to paragraph 6.9.5.1, for M1 and N1 category vehicles, at the discretion of the manufacturer and only if a front side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the front position lamp shall have a horizontal geometric visibility angle of 45° outwards to 45° inwards (the inward angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm).

To be considered visible, the lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 cm2, excluding the illuminating surface of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.
Under the alternative, the front position lamp shall have a vertical visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal (downward angle reducible to 5° if mounted below 750 mm).
The front position lamp shall be oriented forwards.

If the front position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator, its electrical connection on the relevant side may be such that it is switched OFF during the entire time (ON and OFF cycle) of direction-indicator operation.
The electrical connections of the front position lamp shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.

A non-flashing closed-circuit tell-tale for the front position lamps shall be provided, except where the instrument panel lighting can only switch ON simultaneously with the front position lamps or while the daytime running lamps are switched ON; a failure tell-tale is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the front position lamp shall be provided if required by the component regulation.
The front position lamp tell-tale shall be non-flashing and shall not be required if the instrument panel lighting can only switch ON simultaneously with the front position lamps.
The number of side-marker lamps per side shall be such that the rules for longitudinal positioning are complied with.
The side-marker lamps shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 91, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

The side-marker lamp shall be mounted at a height above the ground of not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm).
At least one side-marker lamp shall be fitted to the middle third of the vehicle length.
For M1 vehicles of length exceeding 6 m but not exceeding 7 m, one side-marker lamp fitted not further than 3 m from the front and one within the last third of the vehicle length shall be sufficient.
For vehicles of length not exceeding 6 m, one side-marker lamp fitted within the first third and/or within the last third of the vehicle length shall be sufficient.
The distance between the rearmost side-marker lamp and the rear of the vehicle shall not exceed 1 m.
The distance between two adjacent side-marker lamps shall not exceed 3 m, or 4 m if the structure, design or operational use of the vehicle makes compliance impossible.
The side-marker lamp shall have a horizontal geometric visibility angle of 45° to the front and to the rear; where installation is optional this may be reduced to 30°.
The side-marker lamp shall have a vertical geometric visibility angle of 10° above and below the horizontal, the downward angle being reducible to 5° where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm.

Where side-marker lamps supplement the reduced geometric visibility of front and rear direction indicator lamps and/or position lamps, the angles shall be 45° towards the front and rear ends of the vehicle and 30° towards the centre of the vehicle.
The side-marker lamp shall be oriented towards the side.
On M1 vehicles less than 6 m in length, amber side-marker lamps wired to flash shall flash in phase and at the same frequency as the direction-indicator lamps on the same side of the vehicle.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the side-marker lamp shall be provided if required by the component regulation.

Where an optional side-marker lamp is grouped or combined with a position lamp reciprocally incorporated or grouped with the direction indicator, its electrical connection may be such that it is switched OFF during the entire period (ON and OFF cycle) of direction indicator activation.
For verifying visibility of red light to the front (and white light to the rear), the observation zones shall be bounded in height by horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m above the ground.

For verifying visibility of red light to the front (and white light to the rear), the observation zones shall be bounded in width by two vertical planes forming an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, passing through the contact point(s) of the planes delimiting overall vehicle width.
